task: Fixed256 original player CPU alpha geometry: independent read-only protocol review
status: QA-only pure CPU candidate recommendation; no adoption or execution
sourceFacts: Original raster obtains one pre-weapon256x256 RGBA body array, uses nativeAlphaBounds for global bounds, computes core.height=bounds.height*.72, then calls bodyIdentificationContour on the same array for the upper-body silhouette.
nativeAlphaBounds already searches only inward from each row's left and right edge; it does not visit every interior alpha sample of an occupied row.

bodyIdentificationContour repeats edge searches within the global body x extent for the top..floor(core.y+core.height) rows. A row-endpoint cache can remove that repeated search, not all original alpha reads or the native Canvas readback.
Original contour output requires more than one occupied included row, contains fresh left/right point objects, and top aliases exactly left[0] and right[0].

Original bounds uses alpha<threshold while contour uses alpha>=threshold. These are complementary for finite byte values, but not for generic undefined/NaN values; a generic-array contract cannot be assumed.

proposedPureDomain.input: An attached non-shared Uint8ClampedArray of exactly256*256*4 bytes from the same original successful native body Canvas read. Fixed width/height256, threshold8 and full-image ROI only.
proposedPureDomain.rejectOrFallback: Unsupported width/height, ROI/threshold, detached/shared buffer, non-byte/generic array or untrusted getter-driven input must not be silently treated as equivalent. Preserve the old public helpers and their generic contracts.
proposedPureDomain.oneRowEdgePass: Keep original row ascending order and original left/right alpha comparisons. Store each row's left and right-exclusive endpoints while deriving the same global left/top/right/bottom.
proposedPureDomain.cache: One reusable Uint16Array(512),1024 bytes for256 [left,rightExclusive] pairs. Empty rows use left256/right0; this distinguishes a valid single pixel at x255. Every row must be rewritten each call to prevent stale edges.
proposedPureDomain.bounds: Return the exact original global bounds or the raster's existing empty fallback{x:256,y:256,width:1,height:1}; preserve width/right-exclusive and height/bottom-exclusive arithmetic.
proposedPureDomain.contour: After bounds/core exist, read cached endpoints only for the original included rows. Preserve Math.floor(core.y+core.height), y+.5, right-exclusive coordinates, occupied-row count>1 requirement, fresh output point/array identities and top's aliases. Do not close/fill the torso cutoff or include legs/gun.
proposedPureDomain.outputOwnership: Fresh original-shape bounds/core/contour objects per call. The reusable row buffer remains private and is not embedded in frame/selected/metadata/report or retained by callers.
proposedPureDomain.newAllocations: Contour arrays/point objects remain necessary for original identity and value contracts; do not claim allocation-free output. Only a bounded row cache is added.

savedActualAttribution.scope: Original180 fixed-work A1/A2 with player-only original-call observation. These are historical diagnostic call-wall measurements, not a new performance test or a candidate A/B.
savedActualAttribution.interpretation: The entire raster self remainder is only about0.95%/1.44% of steady callback totals and includes copies/composition, alpha/contour, metadata and observer overhead. Alpha geometry is an unknown smaller subset. Even eliminating this whole measured remainder would not establish a3% whole-callback saving in these samples. The native body-read wait and first GL cost are not removed by CPU row reuse. Inclusive parent/child spans must not be summed.

feasibilityDecision.exactness: Feasible in the narrow byte-array domain without changing source pixels, threshold, bounds, contour shape, draw/read count or quality.
feasibilityDecision.expectedScale: Micro-optimization until independently measured; no existing evidence supports a material whole-frame or whole-app speedup.
feasibilityDecision.productionBoundary: Keep the protected original player and22 original source records unchanged. First implement and prove only a standalone QA CPU helper. A future full-raster candidate requires a deliberate separate task after the pure CPU gate; no product rewrite is justified by a microbench alone.
feasibilityDecision.orderingRiskForLaterRaster: Original contour executes after armed GL/Canvas composition and fallback metadata/frame spreads. Moving contour construction earlier can change behavior if foreign callbacks/getters mutate source state. Any later integration must preserve original ordering where feasible or explicitly restrict to original owned native assets; no universal getter/exception equivalence claim.

focusedOraclePlan: Pin complete original nativeAlphaBounds and production-art module sources as independent oracles. Compare every number with Object.is/IEEE64 representation and every object/array shape, including empty fallback and top alias identities.

Cover alpha0/7/8/255 boundaries, all-empty, full mask, each edge/corner, single x255 pixel, one/two occupied rows, noncontiguous rows, holes, narrow/wide bodies, top/bottom clipping, odd/even heights and every fractional .72 cutoff.
Use deterministic byte masks with RGB noise to prove only alpha controls geometry. Test consecutive populated/empty/narrow masks through one reusable cache to catch stale row state.
Verify input byte array/dimensions/options are never mutated and returned contours from earlier calls do not alias reused cache or later results.
Include meaningful unsupported/detached/shared/generic input behavior without claiming broader old-helper equivalence or silently accepting getter-driven data.

Use real original captured256x256 pre-weapon RGBA for both weapons and representative idle/walk/run/recoil/reload/throw/hit/death/heading poses as independent exact data, not just procedural masks. No assets, clips or animation frames are synthesized.

pureCPUBenchmarkPlan.authority: Root sole executor, after source/oracle freeze and with no concurrent browser/CPU/GPU/test job.
pureCPUBenchmarkPlan.order: One independent-process A1 original-two-functions, B fused-row-cache, A2 original-two-functions bracket with identical Node22 flags and exact input buffer order.
pureCPUBenchmarkPlan.timing: Time only original bounds+core+contour calls versus candidate equivalent calls, including candidate normal guard/cache work and original output allocations. Imports, input loading, hashing, output comparison, report serialization, cleanup and cache/fixture setup are outside timers. First cache initialization is reported separately rather than hidden as a steady win.
pureCPUBenchmarkPlan.coverage: Use the same bounded actual pose buffers and deterministic edge fixtures in all arms, cycle in a fixed order and consume outputs equivalently. Never optimize away outputs or retain an unbounded history.
pureCPUBenchmarkPlan.gate: Predeclare a minimum relative CPU+wall improvement and no output mismatches before execution. Preserve first/all/steady/absolute time per call. A tiny percentage from submillisecond work is a micro result, not proof of whole-frame gain.
pureCPUBenchmarkPlan.claimLimit: 1024 bytes is the explicit reusable CPU row-cache capacity only, not measured total/peak heap, GPU memory or a promise of fewer allocations after JIT. No FPS, GPU-readback or bodyRead wait reduction claim.

nativeQualityBeforeAnyRasterAdoption: On an owned fresh native player, feed each original captured body RGBA array to both original and QA helper outside any cost timing and require exact bounds/core/contour, while preserving the input bytes and original source identity.

If root later authorizes a raster candidate, preserve original one body Canvas read, two GL draws, pre-weapon body image, colour/ink composition and placement. Compare same-pose full body/colour RGBA and metadata strictly at zero tolerance, not merely the reduced geometry DTO.

Whole-scene strict AA/AB/BA, literal Game/events/commands/motion/both RNG and owned cleanup remain separate mandatory gates; historical original-repeat pixel failures are retained and cannot be erased by exact pure geometry.
